newsitem.title: SPAIN: Estonia sees invitation to join EU likely.
newsitem.headline: Estonia sees invitation to join EU likely.

text.p: Estonian President Lennart Meri said on Wednesday that the European Commission was likely to recommend that Estonia be invited to start talks on joining the European Union in its first wave of enlargement.

"We welcome the opinion of the Commission, which however is not official yet, that the Estonians are ready to commence accession negotiations with the European Union," Meri told reporters after a NATO summit in Madrid.
"Many independent analyses confirm this opinion and I am encouraged that it now appears likely that we will be in the first group of new European Union members," he said.
EU officials said on Monday that the Commission was likely to recommend opening membership talks with five eastern European countries including Estonia next week.
A draft prepared by the EU's External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek for discussion by the executive, proposes opening talks with Estonia, Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovenia.
But EU sources said on Wednesday there was resistance to the inclusion of Estonia and Slovenia from powerful elements within the Commission, the 15-member EU's executive body.
"There are still a lot of people in the Commission who want to close the door to the Baltic States and also Slovenia," one official involved in the negotiations told Reuters in Brussels.

Estonian officials denied that EU membership would be a consolation prize for not making the first wave of countries to join NATO. Russia has insisted that the three former Soviet Baltic republics -- Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania -- must not be admitted to the Western military alliance.
"We certainly don't see the EU as a consolation prize. We prefer to keep the two processes separate," one official said.
At a historic summit in Madrid, NATO invited Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary to join the Western alliance but the Baltic states were excluded from the first wave of enlargement.
